zh-CN.title: 如何使用 · 地球公转

lines: 第 1 步：先按「1」定格到春分，看读数区「太阳直射」是多少度。
第 2 步：再按「2」，直射纬度变成 23.5°N —— 这就是北半球夏至。
第 3 步：依次按「3」「4」，对比四个节气的直射点位置。
第 4 步：按「空格」播放，看地球绕太阳走完一圈要多久（有速度调节）。
第 5 步：拖动鼠标换到「俯视」，能看到轨道是个椭圆，地轴始终指向同一方向。
看不到变化？确认顶部「节气定位」已打开，且没有停在暂停状态。
地球绕太阳公转，周期约 365.25 天，轨道近似椭圆，地轴始终指向北极星附近。
地轴与公转轨道面成 66.5° 夹角（赤道面与轨道面夹角 23.5°，即黄赤交角）。
由于地轴倾斜方向不变，太阳直射点在南北回归线之间往返，形成四季更替。
「播放 / 暂停」控制公转动画；「速度」调节一年走完的快慢。
「步进」让地球沿轨道前进一小格，便于逐段观察。
拖动或滚轮改变观察角度与缩放；「俯视 / 侧视」切换视角。
「重置」回到春分起点。
按 1–4 直接定格到春分、夏至、秋分、冬至。
春分 / 秋分：太阳直射赤道（0°），全球昼夜平分。
夏至：直射北回归线 23.5°N，北半球昼最长、北极圈内极昼。
冬至：直射南回归线 23.5°S，北半球昼最短、北极圈内极夜。
定格后读数区显示：公转角度、太阳直射纬度、教材日期、节气名称。
「太阳直射」读数来自模型数据里的 declinationDeg，不是近似公式。
「节气定位」面板列出四个节气的日期与现象说明（中英双语）。
「教学要点」解释：直射点移动 → 正午太阳高度与昼长变化 → 四季。
四季成因是「地轴倾斜且方向不变」，不是「地球离太阳忽远忽近」。
近日点在 1 月初（北半球冬天），远日点在 7 月初（北半球夏天）。
南北半球季节相反：北半球夏至时南半球是冬至。
Esc 关闭窗口，F11 全屏。
Step 1: press 1 to freeze at the spring equinox and read the subsolar latitude.
Step 2: press 2 — the subsolar point jumps to 23.5°N, the June solstice.
Step 3: press 3 and 4 to compare all four key positions.
Step 4: press Space to animate one full orbit; adjust Speed as needed.
Step 5: drag to Top view to see the elliptical orbit and the fixed axis direction.
Nothing changing? Make sure Seasons is on in the top bar and the model isn't paused.
Earth orbits the Sun in ~365.25 days; the axis keeps pointing near Polaris.
The axis is tilted 66.5° to the orbital plane (obliquity 23.5°).
Because the tilt direction is fixed, the subsolar point migrates between the tropics, making seasons.
Key dates: spring equinox 3/21, summer solstice 6/22, autumn equinox 9/23, winter solstice 12/22.
Play/Pause runs the orbit; Speed sets how fast a year passes.
Step advances one increment for close observation.
Drag or scroll to change view/zoom; Top view / Side view switch perspective.
Reset returns to the spring equinox.
Keys 1–4 freeze at spring equinox, summer solstice, autumn equinox, winter solstice.
Equinoxes: subsolar at the equator (0°), equal day and night worldwide.
June solstice: subsolar at 23.5°N; longest day in the north, polar day inside the Arctic Circle.
December solstice: subsolar at 23.5°S; shortest day in the north, polar night.
The readout shows orbit angle, subsolar latitude, textbook date and season name.
Subsolar latitude comes from declinationDeg in the model data, not an approximation.
The seasons panel lists dates and phenomena for all four (bilingual).
Teaching notes: migrating subsolar point → changing noon altitude and day length → seasons.
Seasons come from the fixed axial tilt, NOT from Earth being closer/farther to the Sun.
Perihelion is early January (northern winter); aphelion is early July (northern summer).
Seasons are opposite in the two hemispheres.
Esc closes, F11 toggles fullscreen.
